ORDER Petitioners are traders carrying on various types of business including hotel business.

They have filed these writ petitions seeking direction to the respondents to implement the directions issued by the Apex Court in the matter of MAHARASTRA EKTA HAWKERS` UNION Vs. MUNICIPAL CORPORATION, GREATER MUMBAI, reported in AIR 2004 SC 416.

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioners is that, though the Apex Court has issued guidelines directing the appropriate Government to issue directions with regard to regulating the hawking business, so far,
respondent
No.2 -
Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation has not implemented the directions of the Apex Court.

Petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Maharastra Ekta Hawkers`
Union (referred supra) as well as the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in W.P.
No.14607/2008 dated 04.12.2008, wherein this Court also having regard to the decision of the Apex Court has given direction to all the Municipal Corporations, including Hubli-Dharwad Municipal Corporation to take all necessary and appropriate steps to regulate the hawkers and the footpath shop vendors.

3. It is the case of the petitioners that, they are all traders trading in various businesses after obtaining licences and have invested money in establishing their permanent business and are incurring recurring expenditure towards rent, electricity, water, employment of labourers and tax etc.

However, the act of the respondents allowing the hawkers to carry on their hawking business across the road or in places abutting their permanent establishments has vitally affected their business and thereby, it has denied their fundamental right guaranteed under Articles 19(1)(g) and 21 of the Constitution of India.
Hence, they are before this Court to seek direction to the respondents.

4. During the pendency of these writ petitions, respondent No.2 - Municipal Corporation has filed status report inter alia stating that they have identified the hawking zone and have agreed to implement the directions issued by the Apex Court as well as the Division Bench of this Court.

However, it was submitted that, the hawking zone demarcated would either affect the vehicular Sukumar S/O. Sanjeev Shetty vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25860667/
7 movement or it will go contrary to the guidelines of the Hon`ble Supreme Court.

sentences.text:
Hawkers Association, which is before this Court, has filed an application for impleading in W.P.
No.66400/2012 and their grievance is that the hawking zone has not been properly demarcated.

5. The Apex Court in the decision of MAHARASTRA EKTA HAWKERS` UNION has carved out 16 guidelines, which read as under:
(i) an area of 1 mtr x 1 mtr on one side of the footpath wherever they exist or on an extreme side of the carriage way, in such a manner that the vehicular and pedestrian traffic is not obstructed and access to shops and residences is not blocked.
We further clarify that even where hawking is permitted, it can only be on one side of the footpath or road and under no circumstances on both sides of the footpaths or roads.
We however clarify that Aarey/Sarita stalls and sugar cane vendors would require and may be permitted an area of more than 1 Mt. by 1 Mt. but not more than 2 Mt. by 1 Mt;
(ii) Hawkers must not put up stalls or place any tables, stand or such other thing or erect any type of structure.
They should also not use handcarts.
However they may protect their goods from the sun, rain or wind.
Obviously this condition would not apply to Aarey/sarita stalls;

(iii) There should be no hawking within 100 meters from any place of worship, holy shrine, educational institutions and hospitals or within 150 meters from any municipal or other markets or from any railway station.
There should be no hawking on foot-bridges and over-bridges.
Further certain areas may be required to be kept free of hawkers for security reasons.

However outside places of worship hawkers can be permitted to sell items required by the devotees for offering to the deity or for placing in the place of worship e.g. flowers, sandalwood, candles, agarbattis, coconuts etc.;

(iv) The hawkers must not create any noise or play any instrument or music for attracting the public or the customers;
(v) They can only sell cooked foods, cut fruits juices and the like.
We are unable to accept submission that cooking should be permitted.
We direct that no cooking of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted.
Even where cooked food or cut fruits or the like are sold, the food must not be adulterated or unhygienic.

8 However the payment of prescribed fee shall not be deemed to authorize the hawker to do his business beyond prescribed hours and would not confer on the hawker the right to do business at any particular place;
(viii) The hawkers must extend full cooperation to the municipal conservancy staff for cleaning the streets and footpaths and also to the other municipal staff for carrying on any municipal work.

They must also cooperate with the other Government and public agencies such as BEST undertaking,
Bombay Telephones, BSES Ltd. etc. if they require to lay any cable or any development work.;
( ix) No hawking would be permitted on any street which is less than 8 meters in width.
Further the hawkers also have to comply with Development Control Rules thus there can be no hawking in areas which are exclusively residential and where trading and commercial activity is prohibited.
Thus hawking cannot be permitted on roads and pavements which do not have a shopping line.;
(x) BMC shall grant licences which will have photos of the hawkers on them.
The licence must be displayed, at all times, by the hawkers on their person by clipping it on to their shirt or coat;
(xi) Not more than one member of a family must be given a licence to hawk.
For this purpose BMC will have to computerize its records;

(xii) Vending of costly items e.g. electrical appliances, video and audio tapes and cassettes, cameras,
phones etc are to be prohibited.
In the event of any hawker found to be selling such items his licence must be cancelled forthwith.
(xiii) In areas other than the Non-Hawking Zones, licences must be granted to the hawkers to do their business on payment of the prescribed fee.
The licences must be for a period of 1 year.
That will be without prejudice to the right of the Committee to extend the limits of the Non-Hawking Zones in the interests of public health, sanitation, safety, public convenience and the like.
Hawking licences should not be refused in the Hawking Zones except for good reasons.
The discretion not to grant a hawking licence in the Hawking Zone should be exercised reasonably and in public interest.

(xiv) In future, before making any alteration in the scheme, the Commissioner should place the matter before the Committee who shall take a decision after considering views of all concerned including the hawkers, the Commissioner of Police and members of the public or an association representing the public.
(xv) It is expected that citizens and shopkeepers shall participate in keeping non hawking zones/areas free from hawkers.
They shall do so by bringing to the notice of the concerned ward officer the presence of a hawker in a non hawking zone/area.
The concerned ward officer shall take immediate steps to remove such a hawker.
In case the ward officer takes no action a written complaint may be filed by the citizen/shopkeeper to the Committee.
The Committee shall look into the complaint and if found correct the Committee will with the help of police remove the hawker.
The officer in charge of the concerned police station is directed to give prompt and immediate assistance to the Committee.

6. The object of regulating hawking business is to protect the traders as well as to ensure that hawking business is beneficial for both the traders and hawkers by considering the interest of the permanent traders, hawkers as well as people, who depend on hawking business, without causing health hazards, obstructing pedestrian and the movement of vehicles, etc.,
7.
The guidelines framed by the Apex Court are the general guidelines to be complied by all the Corporations and the concerned local bodies.
However, the conditions, environment and circumstances for each of the Corporation or the local body would be different and requirement would also differ.

It is in this regard, the Commissioner of Police and Commissioner for Hubli-Dharwad Municipal Corporation were requested to be present before the Court to provide proper assistance to evolve reasonable solution for implementing the direction at the earliest.
8.

Though the learned counsel representing the Municipal Corporation submitted that, about 1126 hawkers have been identified in Dharwad city and 2031 hawkers in Hubli city, it is submitted on behalf of the hawkers` association that, there are more than six thousand hawkers in Hubli Dharwad Corporation.
9. The learned counsel appearing for the Municipal Corporation submits that, 7 hawking zones are identified in Dharwad and 21 hawking zones in Hubli City.
Though, initially eight zones were identified in Dharwad City, since one zone was not suitable, it has been dropped.
10. It is not in dispute that, the hawking zones have to be carved out depending on the number of hawkers in both the cities.

While carving out the hawking zone, the respondents have to adhere to the guidelines stated in the judgement of the Apex Court, as understood by the Division Bench of this Court, which are referred to above.

11. At the same time, after identifying the number of hawkers, respondent No.2 - Corporation is required to identify as to how many hawkers possess licenses and now many hawkers are operating without licenses.

In respect of hawkers, who are yet to obtain licence, learned counsel for the Corporation submitted that, they will issue appropriate paper publication for the awareness of the hawkers and give reasonable time to such hawkers to make application for grant of licence and permission.

Similarly, for grant of licenses to the hawkers in respect of food articles under the Sukumar S/O. Sanjeev Shetty vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25860667/
10 provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Regulation 2.1.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011, (for short, `the Regulations`), stipulates that, every petty food business operator is required to register themselves with the Registering Authority.

sentences.text: 12. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Corporation submits that, four months time may be granted for processing and issuing permission and within the said period, if the hawkers had applied for license under the regulation, such application would be disposed in four months time.

13. The learned counsel representing the hawkers Association would submit that, the hawkers would make necessary application for license under the regulation and for permission to Municipal Corporation by complying with all the requirements.

14. Considering the above submission, in the event of the hawkers making such applications, the concerned authority shall dispose of the same within four months as submitted by the learned counsel for the Corporation.
Licensing authority must complete the process of issue of license in the meanwhile.
Since the hawkers` livelihood is dependent on hawking, they shall not be disturbed till such period (i.e., for period of four months).

Once the licensing process is completed within time as stated, in respect of hawkers, who either had not applied or who were not granted with license for not complying with requirement, the Corporation and the other authorities, must take necessary action in accordance with law.

After the period of four months from the date of issue of advertisement, Corporation or other authorities shall not allow the hawker to carry on business without license and permission and also contrary to the directions of the Supreme Court.

15. So far as hawking business in respect of food articles is concerned, the same has direct effect on the public health and maintaining hygienic conditions and providing quality drinking water are of paramount consideration.

16. The Commissioner of the Corporation, who is before this Court submits that, as many as eight R.O. Water supply Centers are provided in Hubli and steps would be taken to provide R.O. water supply centers nearer to the hawking zone and also for general public at bare minimal rate as people, who cannot afford to have mineral water at the market rate can have benefit of quality drinking water at a cheaper rate.

17. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Corporation also submits that, all steps would be taken to prevent health hazards and all necessary facilities would be provided to hawkers depending on the category of vending done by them.

He further submitted that, the process of completing the exercise of identifying hawking zones and regulating business of hawking and also providing facilities to the hawkers would take minimum eight months time as it involves the coordination with the other departments.
Commissioner of Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation requests that eight months time be granted, within which, the Corporation will fully implement the guidelines for regulation of hawking business.

sentences.text: 19. It is made clear that, while implementing the directions of the Hon`ble Supreme Court, the interest of both the hawkers and permanent traders has to be borne in mind.

Hawkers will also abide by the directions of the Hon`ble Supreme Court and they will also abide by the steps taken by the Corporation in getting licences in terms of the conditions stipulated in the Regulations and depending on the number of licences granted to hawkers, the Corporation will decide as to whether the number of hawking zones are to be decreased or increased.
Selection of suitable place for setting up hawking zone shall be made strictly in terms of the directions of the Hon`ble Supreme Court as well as the division Bench of this Court.

20. Keeping all these facts in mind, the Corporation as well as the designated authority for grant of licence under the Regulations and the Commissioner of second respondent - Corporation and the Officers concerned with Traffic and law and order are given eight months time to implement the guide lines of the Hon`ble Supreme Court in Maharastra Ekta Hawkers` Union (referred supra) in regulating hawking business in Dharwad and Hubli.

21. The Commissioner of Corporation, in consultation with the other authorities, shall allocate appropriate area for weekly sandy day to enable the agriculturists to sell their vegetables or any other agricultural produce permitted in law.
22. It is made clear that any business done on footpath should not affect the pedestrian movement and the permission for the same should be granted in accordance with the regulations.
23. By placing the submission of the respondents and their respective counsel on record, writ petitions stands disposed of.
24. Affidavit of undertaking by the concerned authorities shall be filed tomorrow.

opennyai_summary.decision:
14. Considering the above submission, in the event of the hawkers making such applications, the concerned authority shall dispose of the same within four months as submitted by the learned counsel for the Corporation.
Commissioner of Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation requests that eight months time be granted, within which, the Corporation will fully implement the guidelines for regulation of hawking business.
Hawkers will also abide by the directions of the Hon`ble Supreme Court and they will also abide by the steps taken by the Corporation in getting licences in terms of the conditions stipulated in the Regulations and depending on the number of licences granted to hawkers, the Corporation will decide as to whether the number of hawking zones are to be decreased or increased.
Selection of suitable place for setting up hawking zone shall be made strictly in terms of the directions of the Hon`ble Supreme Court as well as the division Bench of this Court.
20. Keeping all these facts in mind, the Corporation as well as the designated authority for grant of licence under the Regulations and the Commissioner of second respondent - Corporation and the Officers concerned with Traffic and law and order are given eight months time to implement the guide lines of the Hon`ble Supreme Court in Maharastra Ekta Hawkers` Union (referred supra) in regulating hawking business in Dharwad and Hubli.
21. The Commissioner of Corporation, in consultation with the other authorities, shall allocate appropriate area for weekly sandy day to enable the agriculturists to sell their vegetables or any other agricultural produce permitted in law.
22. It is made clear that any business done on footpath should not affect the pedestrian movement and the permission for the same should be granted in accordance with the regulations.
23. By placing the submission of the respondents and their respective counsel on record, writ petitions stands disposed of.
24. Affidavit of undertaking by the concerned authorities shall be filed tomorrow.
